scroll-view

Scrollable view area. When the vertical scrolling mode is used, you need to set a fixed height using MASS. The default length unit of component attributes is pixel.

Attribute Type Default Value Mandatory or Not Description
scroll-x Boolean false No Horizontal scrolling.
scroll-y Boolean false No Vertical scrolling.
upper-threshold Number/String 50 No Threshold of the distance to the top or left to trigger the scrolltoupper event.
lower-threshold Number/String 50 No Threshold of the distance to the bottom or right to trigger the scrolltolower event.
scroll-top Number/String No Position of the vertical scrollbar.
scroll-left Number/String No Position of the horizontal scrollbar.
scroll-into-view String No Direction in which an element can be scrolled. The value must be the ID of a subelement. The ID cannot start with a digit.
scroll-with-animation Boolean false No Whether to use animated transitions when setting the position of the scrollbar.
enhanced Boolean false No Whether to enable the scroll-view enhancement feature.
show-scrollbar Boolean true No Whether to display the scrollbar. It is available when the enhanced attribute is enabled.
bindscrolltoupper eventHandle No Triggered when you scroll to the top or left.
bindscrolltolower eventHandle No Triggered when you scroll to the bottom or right.
bindscroll eventHandle No Triggered when scrolling is performed. The output is event.detail = { scrollLeft, scrollTop, scrollHeight, scrollWidth, deltaX, deltaY }.
binddragstart eventHandle No Sliding start event. It is available when the enhanced attribute is enabled. The output is detail { scrollTop, scrollLef }.
binddragging eventHandle No Sliding event. It is available when the enhanced attribute is enabled. The output is detail { scrollTop, scrollLeft }.
binddragend eventHandle No Sliding end event. It is available when the enhanced attribute is enabled. The output is detail { scrollTop, scrollLeft}.

Sample Code

1. Vertical Scroll View

<scroll-view scroll-y="true" style="height: 160px;" bindscrolltoupper="onScrollToUpper" bindscrolltolower="onScrollToLower">
  <view class="scroll-v-item bg-red">Scroll Item 1 (Top)</view>
  <view class="scroll-v-item bg-orange">Scroll Item 2</view>
  <view class="scroll-v-item bg-green">Scroll Item 3</view>
  <view class="scroll-v-item bg-blue">Scroll Item 4 (Bottom)</view>
</scroll-view>
Page({
  onScrollToUpper() { ma.showToast({ title: 'Top Reached', icon: 'none' }); },
  onScrollToLower() { ma.showToast({ title: 'Bottom Reached', icon: 'none' }); }
});
.scroll-v-item { height: 70px; display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; color: #fff; font-weight: 600; margin-bottom: 8px; border-radius: 8px; }
.bg-red { background: #ef4444; } .bg-orange { background: #f97316; } .bg-green { background: #10b981; } .bg-blue { background: #3b82f6; }

2. Horizontal Scroll View

<scroll-view scroll-x="true" style="white-space: nowrap; width: 100%;">
  <view class="scroll-h-item bg-blue">Card 1</view>
  <view class="scroll-h-item bg-green">Card 2</view>
  <view class="scroll-h-item bg-orange">Card 3</view>
  <view class="scroll-h-item bg-purple">Card 4</view>
  <view class="scroll-h-item bg-pink">Card 5</view>
</scroll-view>
Page({ data: {} });
.scroll-h-item { display: inline-block; width: 110px; height: 80px; margin-right: 10px; border-radius: 8px; text-align: center; line-height: 80px; color: #fff; font-weight: 600; }
.bg-purple { background: #8b5cf6; } .bg-pink { background: #ec4899; }

Bug & Tip

  1. The priority of scroll-into-view is higher than that of scroll-top. scroll-into-view is valid only in the initial state.

  2. When scroll-view is scrolled, the page is prevented from rebounding. Therefore, when scroll-view is scrolled, the onPullDownRefresh hook function cannot be called.

  3. To use the drop-down refresh, you need to use the scrolling of the page instead of scroll-view. In this case, you can return to the top of the page by clicking the top status bar.
